title: Work out the group
one: Three scores become one group, worked out by a piece of code you name yourself.

next.title: Save the details to the file

screens.title: Check the parts this chapter needs
screens.goal: Before I start, I check the Load event, the group panel, Global.cs and my task sheet.

blocks.p: This chapter uses work from earlier chapters. This screen checks that it is there.

check.what: Is the data entry Load event done, so the group panel switches on after the test?
check.how: Run the program. Take the quiz and the test. Look at the group panel.

check.what: Does the group panel have a result box and a Calculate button?
check.how: Open frmDataEntry in the Design tab. Look inside the group panel.

check.what: Is YOUR task sheet open at the page with the bands and the group names?
check.how: Find the page that says which scores give which group.
check.fix: Ask your teacher for the task sheet.

stages.title: Your own piece of code, with a name you choose

screens.title: Write your own code that picks the group
screens.goal: I write a piece of code by hand, give it a name, and it turns three numbers into one group.

blocks.p: Until now, each [[method|0]] came from double-clicking a button. This one you write by hand.
You choose its name. That makes it a [[user-defined method|1]].

words: A named piece of code that runs when it is asked to.
A method you write and name yourself.
blocks.intro: Two new words in this chapter. Click a marked word to see what it means.

drawn.name: CalculateGroup
drawn.alt: Three numbers, 3, 2 and 3, drop into a box called CalculateGroup. The word Advanced comes out.
drawn.say: Three bands go in. One group comes out.

blocks.watch: The button code on stage 3 works out the three bands. Then it asks CalculateGroup for the group.

screens.title: Type the first line, the total and the first group
screens.goal: CalculateGroup takes in three whole numbers, adds them up, and hands back Weak when the total is 4 or less.

blocks.p: Scroll to the bottom of frmDataEntry's code. Click the empty line above the last two curly brackets.

code.title: CalculateGroup, part 1 of 2
code.where: above the last two curly brackets of frmDataEntry's code
partLines: The first line, typed by you
private means only this form uses it. string means it hands back words. Then its name and three whole numbers coming in.
Add them up
The three numbers are added into total. Then an empty line.
Four or less is Weak
If the total is 4 or less, return hands back the word Weak.
code.yours: MY bands and group names come from MY task. Use the numbers and names on YOUR task sheet.

blocks.watch: No double-click makes this first line. Type every word of it yourself.

screens.title: Hand back the other two groups
screens.goal: A total of 7 or less hands back Intermediate, and anything more hands back Advanced.

blocks.p: Each return hands the answer back to the code that asked for it.

code.title: CalculateGroup, part 2 of 2
partLines: Seven or less is Intermediate
Otherwise, if the total is 7 or less, hand back Intermediate.
Anything more is Advanced
Every other total hands back Advanced.
Close it
An empty line, then the curly bracket that ends CalculateGroup.
code.yours: MY numbers are 4 and 7, and MY groups are Weak, Intermediate and Advanced. Type the ones on YOUR task sheet.

screens.title: Stop if anything is not done yet
screens.goal: If the quiz, the test or the average is not done, or the details are not entered, a message shows and the code stops.

blocks.p: In the Design tab, double-click the Calculate button in the group panel.

code.title: The Calculate button, part 1 of 7
code.where: between the curly brackets of btnCalculateSwimmingGroup_Click
partLines: Visual Studio wrote these two lines
Leave them as they are. Your code goes between the curly brackets.
given
Not everything done? Stop here
If any of the four is not done, a message shows. Then the code stops.
Notes for you
An empty line, then three notes about the scores. They do not run.

blocks.watch: Line 3 is one long line. Keep it on one line in Visual Studio.

screens.title: Make room for three bands
screens.goal: When everything is done, three whole numbers start at 0, one for each band.

blocks.p: A band is 1, 2 or 3. Each score gets a band on the next screens.

code.title: The Calculate button, part 2 of 7
partLines: Otherwise, carry on
Two empty lines, then else and its curly bracket.
Three bands to fill
One whole number for each band. Each starts at 0.
A note for the quiz
An empty line, then a note. The quiz band comes next.

screens.title: Give the quiz score a band
screens.goal: A quiz score of 1 or less is band 1, 3 or less is band 2, and anything more is band 3.

blocks.p: The same shape of question as in CalculateGroup. This time each answer is a band.

code.title: The Calculate button, part 3 of 7
partLines: One or less is band 1
If the quiz score is 1 or less, the quiz band is 1.
Three or less is band 2
Otherwise, if it is 3 or less, the quiz band is 2.
Anything more is band 3
Every other score makes the quiz band 3.
code.yours: MY quiz is out of 5, so MY numbers are 1 and 3. YOUR task sheet gives YOURS.

screens.title: Give the test score a band
screens.goal: A test score of 1 or less is band 1, and 4 or less is band 2.

blocks.p: The test band has the same shape. This screen does bands 1 and 2.

code.title: The Calculate button, part 4 of 7
partLines: A note for the test
An empty line, then a note.
One or less is band 1
If the test score is 1 or less, the test band is 1.
Four or less is band 2
Otherwise, if it is 4 or less, the test band is 2.
code.yours: MY numbers are 1 and 4. Use the numbers on YOUR task sheet.

screens.title: The last test band
screens.goal: Any other test score is band 3.

blocks.p: The last part of the test band, then a note for the average.

code.title: The Calculate button, part 5 of 7
partLines: Anything more is band 3
Every other score makes the test band 3. An empty line sits inside.
A note for the average
An empty line, then a note. The average band comes next.

screens.title: Give the average a band
screens.goal: An average under 4 is band 1, 7 or less is band 2, and anything more is band 3.

blocks.p: Look closely at the first line. It says less than 4, not 4 or less.

code.title: The Calculate button, part 6 of 7
partLines: Under 4 is band 1
If the average is less than 4, the average band is 1.
Seven or less is band 2
Otherwise, if it is 7 or less, the average band is 2.
Anything more is band 3
Every other average makes the band 3.
code.yours: MY numbers are 4 and 7. Use the numbers on YOUR task sheet.

screens.title: Ask for the group and grey out the panel
screens.goal: CalculateGroup turns the three bands into a group, Global.cs remembers it and the group panel goes grey.

flow.say: The group panel goes grey. Save comes next.

code.title: The Calculate button, part 7 of 7
partLines: Ask CalculateGroup
The three bands go in. The group comes out into the box.
Remember it, grey the panel
Global.cs keeps the group. The group panel switches off.
Close the else
The end of else, then two empty lines.
Visual Studio wrote this line
This curly bracket is the end. Your code goes above it.
given

screens.title: Try your Calculate button
screens.goal: I run the program, do everything, and check the group, the grey panel and two sets of scores.

blocks.p: Run your program. Log in, enter the details, the attempts, the quiz and the test. Then try each row.

check.how: A group appears in the box. The group panel goes grey.

check.what: Run again. Get all 5 quiz questions right. Click 6 winning pictures. Type 8, 8 and 8 as the attempts.
check.how: Click Calculate. MY bands give Advanced. YOURS give YOUR top group.

check.what: Run again. Get 1 quiz question right. Click 1 winning picture. Type 2, 2 and 2 as the attempts.
check.how: Click Calculate. MY bands give Weak. YOURS give YOUR lowest group.

check.what: After the group appears, click Calculate again.
check.how: Nothing must happen, because the panel is grey.
check.fix: If something happens, look at screen 3-7.
